reason: The hypothesis relies on specific claims about a dual-phase oxide/phosphate coating, its adaptive tribofilm mechanism, and its performance on a CoCrFeNi substrate. The cited evidence (E1, E2) does not address any of these key premises: E1 concerns a different HEA film (AlCrTiZrMo) and its oxidation/tribocorrosion at 800 °C, while E2 describes room-temperature tribological test conditions for a different HEA lubricant on steel. Neither provides support for the proposed coating design, mechanism, or predicted performance on CoCrFeNi.
premises: A dual-phase coating with inert oxide and reactive glassy phosphate phases can form an adaptive tribofilm across RT–800 °C.
A graded interface ensures coating adhesion and integrity over the full temperature range.
The proposed mechanism (glassy phase dominant at low T; oxide network with glassy binder at high T) is plausible for CoCrFeNi.
The coating will reduce friction by ≥30% and significantly lower wear versus uncoated CoCrFeNi across the full range.
The cited evidence supports the feasibility of such a coating on a HEA substrate.
